solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I'm surprised by refusal to back name-giver

indicators.note: to back is read as to go backwards, so the joined words are turned around

parts.note: the exclamation 'My!' expresses surprise
nope is a casual refusal

explanation.surface: Someone startled when the person who named something refuses to support it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' reverses MY + NOPE (MYNOPE) as one string.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym is the person whose name is given to something, such as a place or invention.

clue.text: After drink, Englishman abroad welcomes plug for Indian food

indicators.note: after sets the order: the drink comes first, the rest after it

parts.note: pop is a fizzy drink

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pom is Australian slang for an English person
an ad is an advert, a plug

explanation.surface: After a drink, an expat Englishman welcomes a plug for an Indian dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A poppadom is a thin crisp lentil wafer served with Indian meals.

clue.text: Ornament put away rapidly on spike

parts.note: to neck a drink is to gulp it down
to lace a drink is to spike it

explanation.surface: An ornament quickly stowed on a spike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' and 'spike' both turn out to be about drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklace is jewellery worn round the neck, an ornament.

clue.text: Visitors arrived in greater numbers around British seaside resort

indicators.note: around says the phrase wraps round the single letter

parts.note: more came

explanation.surface: Tourists flocked to a British seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: MORECAMBE is a seaside town in Lancashire, north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Morecambe is a resort town on Morecambe Bay in Lancashire.

clue.text: Model soldier like millions

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
to dig something is slang for to like it
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A toy soldier modelled to look like millions of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' is a verb here, as in 'I dig that'.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradigm is a typical example or pattern, a template that others follow.

clue.text: After sectarian conflict, dispatch part of army deployment

parts.note: to post is to dispatch
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a formation is a deployment of troops

explanation.surface: After fighting between sects, send off a section of the army.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reformation was the 16th-century split between Catholics and Protestants.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-Reformation describes the period following the Reformation, a religious schism.

clue.text: Supporter lost ground in a sport

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the sport

parts.note: PE is physical education, school sport

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: A backer lost ground in a sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost ground' reads as falling behind, but 'ground' means crushed and gives OSTL; PE is school sport.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a passionate advocate of a cause.

clue.text: Wrong about temperature, which won't be perishing

indicators.note: about places the wrong word around the single letter

parts.note: immoral means morally wrong

explanation.surface: Mistaken about how cold it is: it won't be freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perishing' looks like 'freezing cold' beside temperature, but means dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immortal never dies, so it will never perish.

clue.text: Lucifer may be here, game to fight

parts.note: a match is a game
to box is to fight

explanation.surface: The Devil might lurk here, a game to fight over.
explanation.walkthrough: A lucifer is an old word for a match, not just Satan.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucifer is an early friction match, so it is kept in a matchbox.

clue.text: European Pope defending rogue pleasure-seeker

indicators.note: defending pictures one word standing guard around another, enclosing it

parts.note: Pius is the name of several popes
a cur is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A European pope protecting a scoundrel who lives for pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defending' reads as protecting, but here it means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek philosopher Epicurus taught that pleasure is the highest good, hence 'epicurean'.

clue.text: Male with head turning for Sally

indicators.note: turning means the joined pieces are read in the other direction

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
nob is slang for head

explanation.surface: A man whose head keeps swivelling towards a woman called Sally.
explanation.walkthrough: TOMNOB turned around gives the answer. 'Sally' looks like a woman's name but is a witty remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quick witty retort, which is what a bon mot is.

clue.text: One's inclined to travel in this vehicle and clear off

definitions.text: One's inclined to travel in this

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone bad or astray, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone keen to ride in this vehicle and then clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges CLEAR into LECAR. 'inclined' looks like 'keen' but means on a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable car hauls passengers up and down steep slopes, so its riders travel on an incline.

clue.text: Virtuous person knowing formal behaviour

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST
arch means slyly knowing

explanation.surface: A good person who sees through stiff etiquette.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch figuratively means stiffness or rigid formality of manner.

clue.text: Something burning affected tree close to copse

parts.note: camp means exaggeratedly affected
a fir is a conifer

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Something alight has damaged a tree near a small wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' looks like 'harmed' but means showy.
explanation.definitionFit: A campfire is an outdoor fire kept burning at a campsite.

clue.text: Touching new peach, extremely gentle heat

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: new says the letters take a fresh form
extremely means at the extremes, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A newly ripe peach is touchingly mild yet very warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns PEACH into PECHA. 'heat' is a race, not warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: A repechage is an extra qualifying race, a heat giving losers a second chance.

clue.text: Duck appears from the east without its head

indicators.note: read from the east is read right to left, so the letters run backwards
losing its head means its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: appears means seems

explanation.surface: A headless duck turns up from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEMS loses its first letter ('without its head'), giving EEMS, which 'from the east' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Smee is a sea duck, the smew; it is a crossword staple for 'duck'.

clue.text: Sweet course not finished by bishop

indicators.note: not finished means the word stops short, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a syllabus is a course of study
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A dessert course left uneaten by the bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like part of a meal but is a study programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabub is a creamy dessert of whipped cream and wine, a sweet.

clue.text: I'm not sure highly colourful clothes will be for the general public

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the word dresses another, holding it inside

parts.note: exotic means strikingly colourful and unusual
er is a hesitant sound of doubt

explanation.surface: Someone doubting whether loud clothes suit ordinary folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb, not garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Exoteric teaching is meant for outsiders and the many, unlike esoteric.

clue.text: After alcohol, kiss boy or girl

parts.note: ale is beer
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: After a drink, a kiss from a boy or girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just sets the order: ALE comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Alex is a short name used for both sexes, from Alexander or Alexandra.

clue.text: With poles, carrying current mechanical beings

parts.note: and means with, plus

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: rods are poles
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Robots with poles that conduct electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Androids are robots built in human form.

clue.text: Release men thus possessing a legal right

indicators.note: possessing says the phrase holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Freeing men because they have a legal right.
explanation.definitionFit: An easement is a legal right over another's land, such as a right of way.

clue.text: Reptile quietly buried in ground

indicators.note: something buried in the ground sits inside it, so the letter goes within

parts.note: terrain is ground
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A reptile lies quietly buried in the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, a reptile.

clue.text: Rest breaks around bad climbing frame

indicators.note: around places the jumbled letters round the turned piece
breaks means the word is broken up and its letters reset
in a down entry climbing means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ill means bad

explanation.surface: Taking pauses on a poorly made climbing frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' gives TRES and 'climbing' gives LLI. 'climbing frame' reads as one playground item, but only 'frame' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice frame that supports climbing plants.

clue.text: Bow milliner, perhaps, put on line second

parts.note: a hatter is a milliner; someone from Bow, in London's Cockney East End, drops the H: 'atter

explanation.surface: A milliner placing a hat on a line, then a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' places the 'ATTER after L in a down-the-line sense of charade order. Bow is in the East End, where Cockneys drop their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Of two things the latter is the second one mentioned.

clue.text: Damned instigator of riot has charged around

indicators.note: around says the longer word wraps round the single letter

parts.note: charged with a crime is accused

indicators.note: the instigator starts things, so the word's first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A rioter's ringleader has been charged and cursed for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Accursed and damned are synonyms: under a curse, doomed.

clue.text: Just bank on reversal of rating

indicators.note: reversal of plainly asks for the next word's letters backwards

parts.note: an AB (able seaman) is a naval rating
to bank on is to rely

explanation.surface: Depending on a ratings downgrade, just about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' looks like a score but is an ordinary sailor; 'reversal of' gives BA.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and barely both mean by a narrow margin, only just.

clue.text: Fancied a military man in tight denim

indicators.note: in puts the article and soldier inside the jumbled letters
tight is slang for drunk, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in skinny jeans was fancied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' looks like a fit of jeans but means drunk, scrambling to IMNED.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to imagine it, as in 'fancy that'.

clue.text: Rugby player's leg with which ball may be struck

definitions.text: with which ball may be struck

parts.note: a back is a rugby position; the 's adds S
pins is slang for legs, so a pin is a leg

explanation.surface: A rugby player's leg used to strike the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Backspin is the reverse rotation put on a ball by striking it low, as in tennis or snooker.

clue.text: Gutted, Edgar was on the bench, perhaps an unknown substitute

indicators.note: a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: someone on a bench sat
Z is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Edgar was gutted to sit on the bench, perhaps as an unknown substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' looks like 'upset' but strips EDGAR to ER. 'perhaps' flags sitting on a bench as one way to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior replacement standing in for the real thing.
